evidence: Brief and all three notes keep one consistent first-person voice of a small-firm requester (we/our, occasionally I), with reasons attached to requirements rather than a spec cadence. instruction.md:1 'our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last'; instruction.md:3 'Two things matter more than anything else.'; instruction.md:9 'please try it the way we'll use it ... and make sure nothing breaks.' Notes give user reasons in the same voice: conversations.md:5 'Our clients ask several things at once, so answers have to stay with their question.'; conversations.md:9 'People fix typos and figures, so authors can edit...'; conversations.md:13 'Clients paste all sorts into chat'; conversations.md:29 'Our internet in court is patchy.' (terse fragment-style line); conversations.md:31 'That must not disturb what I'm doing'; walls-and-retention.md:59 'A wall has to be airtight, because a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us.'; integration.md:40 'which is why we care that the order stays consistent.' Mechanical checks: grep for marketing gloss (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamline|utilize) across instruction.md and notes = 0 hits; 14 contractions (we'll, doesn't, can't, mustn't, I'm, isn't, aren't...); 0 em dashes; no bulleted/parallel acceptance lists (only one account table, walls-and-retention.md:47-53, which is a natural way to hand over logins). Sentence length varies from 4-word lines to long explanatory sentences. integration.md is more technical (Node 22, NODE_PATH, DB_PATH) but stays in the 'We start the app...' / 'so we can tell the server itself is up' voice, so no voice change between brief and notes. Broken-alternative probe: a rewrite in 'The system shall provide...' or bulleted MUST lists, or gloss such as 'seamless, robust real-time experience', would fail this row; none present. Conforming-alternative probe: a reviewer could object to long enumerations (walls-and-retention.md:59 list of leak routes; conversations.md:13 'in the thread, in a reply's quote, in search snippets, in earlier versions and in transcripts') as polished; they are written as a single run-on sentence with a stated reason, not parallel bullets, and the exhaustive-coverage question belongs to row 1 (natural product request), not voice. Minor I/we alternation (conversations.md:25, :31) reads as a real person writing, not a defect. No runtime evidence is required for this text-only row.
